item.title: The Pipeline from Human Interaction to System Output
item.lead: The dossier describes a technical transition where human chat does not disappear but is embedded in a pipeline of profile data, scripts, dashboards, and AI tools.

blocks.text: In the source, the workflow consists of multiple layers: user data is collected in CRM, scripts structure the conversation, chatters perform the interaction, and AI can suggest texts or next steps. The effect is a hybrid system in which human and machine together produce the behavior that the user experiences as a personal conversation.

The central technical advantage is repeatability. A human operator can learn from previous conversations; a CRM can store those lessons; a model can then generate similar formulations. As a result, knowledge shifts from the individual to the system. What starts today as the experience of one chatter can be reused tomorrow as a template.

The dossier refers to this as a form of "scalable intimacy." The term is deliberately paradoxical: intimacy is normally contextual and personal, whereas scalability precisely requires standardization. The technical system attempts to resolve this tension by concealing standardization so effectively that the interaction continues to feel personal.

For the analysis of AI, it is therefore insufficient to ask whether an answer was written by a human or a machine. More important is what data the system uses, which objectives it optimizes, and what information the user receives about it.

blocks.label: TECHNICAL CORE
blocks.text: In this dossier, AI primarily changes not the content of intimacy, but its scale, speed, and reproducibility.
